Here is my structured code review report:\n\n---\n\n# Code Review Report: MyMouseBattery\n\n## 1. CRITICAL Issues (Must Fix)\n\n### 1.1 Notification tracking is completely broken — Device ID regenerates every refresh\n**File:** `BatteryService.swift:64-68`\n```swift\nlet device = DeviceBattery(\n    id: UUID().uuidString,  // ← PROBLEM: New ID every time\n    name: productName,\n    batteryLevel: batteryPercent,\n    deviceType: deviceType\n)\n```\n**Description:** `detectDevices()` creates a fresh `UUID().uuidString` each time it runs. `NotificationService` uses `device.id` in its `notifiedDevices` Set (line 36). Since the ID changes on every refresh, `notifiedDevices` can never retain a device across refresh cycles. This means:\n- Notifications will fire repeatedly for the same device\n- The \"reset notified devices\" feature won't work because IDs never match\n- The logic at lines 41-42 (`if level > notificationThreshold { notifiedDevices.remove(device.id) }`) can never trigger\n\n**Fix:** Derive stable ID from device properties (e.g., hash of `productName` + `deviceType`) or use `IORegistryEntryID` if available.\n\n---\n\n### 1.2 NotificationService is never called — dead code\n**File:** `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:35-39`\n```swift\nbatteryService.onDevicesUpdated = { [weak self] in\n    DispatchQueue.main.async {\n        self?.updateStatusItemImage()  // ← Only updates icon\n    }\n}\n```\n**Description:** `onDevicesUpdated` callback only updates the status item image. It never calls `notificationService.checkBatteryLevels(for:)`. The entire `NotificationService` logic (lines 30-44) is unreachable dead code.\n\n**Fix:** Call `notificationService.checkBatteryLevels(for: batteryService.devices)` in the callback.\n\n---\n\n### 1.3 Service instance mismatch between AppDelegate and SwiftUI views\n**File:** `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:7-8` vs `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:25-26`\n```swift\n// In SwiftUI App struct:\n@StateObject private var notificationService = NotificationService()\n@StateObject private var launchAtLoginService = LaunchAtLoginService()\n\n// In AppDelegate (DIFFERENT instances):\nprivate var notificationService: NotificationService { NotificationService() }\nprivate var launchAtLoginService: LaunchAtLoginService { LaunchAtLoginService() }\n```\n**Description:** AppDelegate's computed properties create new instances each access, completely separate from the `@StateObject` instances in SwiftUI. Settings changed in `SettingsView` won't affect `AppDelegate`'s notification service. Changes to `launchAtLoginService.isEnabled` in one place won't be reflected in the other.\n\n**Fix:** Use `BatteryService.shared.notificationService` and `BatteryService.shared.launchAtLoginService` — shared singletons, not per-access instantiated objects.\n\n---\n\n### 1.4 Hardened Runtime disabled\n**File:** `project.yml:27`\n```yaml\nENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME: NO\n```\n**Description:** Hardened Runtime is disabled. This is a security risk and will cause issues with notarization. macOS 12+ requires hardened runtime for App Store distribution.\n\n**Fix:** Set to `YES` and add necessary entitlements.\n\n---\n\n### 1.5 Thread-unsafe access to `notifiedDevices` and `devices`\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:11-12`\n```swift\nprivate var notifiedDevices: Set<String> = []\nprivate var devices: [DeviceBattery] = []\n```\n**Description:** `notifiedDevices` is accessed from:\n- `checkBatteryLevels` (synchronously)\n- `sendNotification` completion handler (async callback)\n- `resetNotifiedDevices` (sync)\n\nNo synchronization. `devices` is set in `checkBatteryLevels` but also potentially accessed elsewhere. Swift's `Set` is not thread-safe for concurrent access.\n\n**Fix:** Use a serial `DispatchQueue` or `actor` for all access to `notifiedDevices` and `devices`.\n\n---\n\n## 2. HIGH Issues (Should Fix)\n\n### 2.1 `print()` used for error logging — no structured logging\n**Files:** `BatteryService.swift:158`, `NotificationService.swift:25,61`\n```swift\nprint(\"Error updating launch at login: \\(error)\")\nprint(\"Notification authorization error: \\(error)\")\nprint(\"Failed to send notification: \\(error)\")\n```\n**Description:** Uses `print()` for error conditions. No `os.Logger`, no log levels, no persistence. Errors are invisible in production.\n\n**Fix:** Replace with `Logger(subsystem: \"com.magicmousebattery.app\", category: \"...\")` using Swift's os.log API.\n\n---\n\n### 2.2 No error feedback to user for notification failures\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:59-62`\n```swift\nUNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) { error in\n    if let error = error {\n        print(\"Failed to send notification: \\(error)\")  // ← Silent failure\n    }\n}\n```\n**Description:** If a notification fails (e.g., permission denied), the user is never informed. They simply won't receive low battery alerts.\n\n**Fix:** Show an alert or update UI to inform user of notification permission issues.\n\n---\n\n### 2.3 Authorization error also swallowed\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:23-26`\n```swift\nUNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound, .badge]) { granted, error in\n    if let error = error {\n        print(\"Notification authorization error: \\(error)\")\n    }\n}\n```\n**Description:** If authorization fails, user is not informed. App won't send notifications and user won't know why.\n\n---\n\n### 2.4 Magic strings for UserDefaults keys\n**Files:** `BatteryService.swift:130`, `NotificationService.swift:7,15`, `LaunchAtLoginService.swift:136,130`\n\n**Description:** Keys like `\"launchAtLogin\"`, `\"notificationThreshold\"` are scattered across files. Risk of typos and inconsistency.\n\n**Fix:** Create a `UserDefaultsKeys` enum or struct with static constants:\n```swift\nenum UserDefaultsKeys {\n    static let launchAtLogin = \"launchAtLogin\"\n    static let notificationThreshold = \"notificationThreshold\"\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.5 No notification permission check before sending\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:47-63`\n```swift\nprivate func sendNotification(for device: DeviceBattery) {\n    // No check if notifications are authorized\n    let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()\n    ...\n    UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) { ... }\n}\n```\n**Description:** Sends notification without checking if authorization was granted. Will silently fail if permission denied.\n\n**Fix:** Check `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getNotificationSettings()` before sending.\n\n---\n\n## 3. MEDIUM Issues (Consider Fixing)\n\n### 3.1 Deprecated `lockFocus`/`unlockFocus` for image resizing\n**File:** `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:58-65`\n```swift\nlet resizedImage = NSImage(size: NSSize(width: 18, height: 18))\nresizedImage.lockFocus()\nimage.draw(in: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: resizedImage.size),\n          from: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: image.size),\n          operation: .sourceOver,\n          fraction: 1.0)\nresizedImage.unlockFocus()\n```\n**Description:** `lockFocus`/`unlockFocus` are deprecated since macOS 10.14. Also, the resized image quality may be poor — no interpolation settings.\n\n**Fix:** Use `NSImage(size:flipped:drawingHandler:)` or `NSImage.draw(in:afterOperationIn:)` with proper caching.\n\n---\n\n### 3.2 No version synchronization between project.yml and Info.plist\n**Files:** `project.yml:10` vs `Info.plist:19-22`\n```yaml\n# project.yml\nMARKETING_VERSION: \"1.0.0\"\n\n# Info.plist\n<key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key>\n<string>1.0.0</string>\n```\n**Description:** Version defined in two places. Risk of drift.\n\n**Fix:** Use Xcode Gen's `info.properties` to reference `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` or generate Info.plist from project.yml.\n\n---\n\n### 3.3 Hardcoded Spanish strings — no localization\n**Files:** `SettingsView.swift:9,15,23,42,55`, `MenuBarView.swift:13,39,52,68`\n\n**Description:** All UI text is hardcoded in Spanish. No `.strings` files for localization. Not accessible to non-Spanish users.\n\n**Fix:** Use `String(localized:)` with `.strings` files for localization support.\n\n---\n\n### 3.4 BatteryService timer not properly managed\n**File:** `BatteryService.swift:20-22`\n```swift\ndeinit {\n    timer?.invalidate()\n}\n```\n**Description:** `BatteryService` is a singleton — it will never be deallocated.
